Meeting Header:

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for blocking out the hour um this is Jordan from Redwood, i'll kick it off. we wanted to frame the sprint and make sure we have clear success criteria and owners.
[00:15] Lisa: thanks Jordan, yeah from product side we just want predictable latency and keep costs under the 60k monthly cap for the pilot, otherwise we'll have to pull back.
[00:28] Amir: quick note, our production tail latency last week hit 1.2s at p95 on some long-context flows, that's what kicked off this conversation, plus a 30% usage uptick from a feature test.
[00:41] Priya: okay, thanks Amir. that's helpful. can you tell us the seq len distribution and which model variant you're currently using?
[00:52] Amir: sure, mostly 128 tokens avg, spikes to ~512 for our summarization path. we're on an open-llama-ish model (we call it BA-13B) running on mixed-precision, but we do quantize for some cheaper endpoints.
[01:08] Marco: and just to add we saw CPU wait and NVLink queuing at times during the spike, so some requests got queued at the service side, not sure if it's the runtime batching.
[01:23] Priya: got it. sounds like there might be batching mis-config or long KV cache warmups. we'll propose config changes.
[01:35] Sofia: quick administrative, we'll need to share SOC2 docs and KMS integration steps. Marco, is BlueArc planning VPC peering or will you go via private endpoints?
[01:48] Marco: prefer VPC peering for now, but we need your peering CIDR and a few firewall rules.
[01:56] Jordan: we'll get that list in the next 48 hours.
[02:02] Lisa: on costs — Hannah is here — we have a firm quarter budget and can't exceed it; we need scenarios with reserved capacity and burst buffers so we can see tradeoffs.
[02:15] Hannah: correct, we can stretch a little if ROI looks good but need transparency in per-token and per-hour reserved costs.
[02:26] Jordan: understood. Priya, can you walk through the proposed benchmark and what metrics we'll collect?
[02:33] Priya: yes— we'll run a 72-hour benchmark on a dedicated-lb cluster mirroring their production seq length mix and concurrency. collect p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, GPU utilization, context switch rates, cost per 1M tokens under various batch sizes, and KV cache hit ratio. we'll also test fallbacks to smaller quantized models to measure quality loss.
[02:56] Amir: when you say "dedicated-lb" do you mean reserved capacity with autoscale? we don't have infra to manage model servers ourselves.
[03:07] Priya: yes reserved capacity on Redwood Dedicated with autoscale rules that you control. for the pilot we can run short bursts to simulate peak load.
[03:16] Marco: how do we confirm data residency and logs? we need full audit logs and optional log retention in our account.
[03:26] Sofia: we can enable audit-logs export to your S3 and show the schema. KMS integration supports both customer-managed keys and Redwood-managed; we'll share the setup steps.
[03:38] Lisa: who's responsible for the compliance review? we have internal security signoff needed.
[03:44] Sofia: i can be the point for documents; Priya will handle the technical bits for the security team.
[03:51] Jordan: okay, so tentative success criteria: p95 < 500ms for chat paths, p95 < 1s for long-context summarization, cost below forecasted cap, and no data egress beyond agreed regions. sound right?
[04:07] Lisa: yes those look like the right gates.
[04:11] Amir: one question — what about fallback behavior if Dedicated capacity is saturated? do we have automatic routing to hosted variants?
[04:20] Priya: yes we support policy-based routing; we can set cost-limited fallback to a smaller quantized model in another region or to hosted endpoints with slightly higher cost but preserved availability. we'll show sample configs.
[04:34] Marco: any throttling visibility? we need token-level billing and realtime alerts.
[04:40] Jordan: console provides token-level breakdown, and we'll configure alerts for rate-limit nearing and error spikes.
[04:47] Hannah: about pricing, can you outline reserved vs on-demand math quickly?
[04:52] Jordan: sure — at a high level, reserved is cheaper per-hour once usage is steady; with burst credit you can absorb spikes. we'll send a detailed spreadsheet.
[05:02] Lisa: ok, two practical asks: (1) show us how much we'd save at 60k cap vs current pattern, (2) show worst-case overage impact so finance can model burn.
[05:12] Jordan: we'll run both scenarios.
[05:15] Amir: for the benchmark, you'll need our top-20 prompts and traces. I'll collate and drop them in the shared folder.
[05:22] Marco: and i will share peering info.
[05:26] Priya: for the bench we'll also capture model perplexity/quality delta when moving to quantized variants — to ensure we don't degrade customer experience beyond an agreed threshold.
[05:37] Lisa: how long do we expect the sprint? you said 4 weeks?
[05:40] Jordan: yes, 4 weeks with weekly checkpoints and a decision at the end.
[05:44] Sofia: i'll schedule recurring meetings Tuesdays 10am PT — and we'll prep a short deck for each checkpoint.
[05:51] Hannah: quick question on invoices — if we go reserved, do you require annual commit or monthly?
[05:58] Jordan: reserved can be monthly or annual; monthly reserved gives flexibility but slightly higher unit price. we'll outline both.
[06:06] Amir: any risk of model performance regressions when you swap kernels/quantization for cheaper endpoints?
[06:13] Priya: there's always tradeoffs — we'll quantify via eval prompts and run A/B comparisons during the bench.
[06:20] Lisa: okay good. two small items: can you share a test account with lower-cost tokens so our dev team can run integration tests without affecting prod spend?
[06:31] Jordan: yes, we can provision a dev key with quota limits. Sofia will own getting that into your dev team.
[06:37] Sofia: noted.
[06:40] Marco: timeline: we'll try to have traces + peering info by Friday.
[06:44] Amir: i can start tonight.
[06:46] Jordan: perfect. we'll follow up with an email recap and attach the benchmark plan and cost-model spreadsheet.
[06:55] Lisa: last question — metrics we care about for acceptance: latency SLOs, cost delta vs baseline, audit-log integrity, and any regressions in model outputs.
[07:08] Priya: we'll map those to concrete pass/fail thresholds in the bench doc.
[07:12] Jordan: alright, thanks everyone. we'll reconvene next Tuesday 10am PT.
[07:18] (meeting ends)
